chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yaqoub ibn Yaqteen, who said:
Abu Al-Hasan Al-Reza (peace be upon him) said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Make your bread small, for with each loaf is a blessing.'
And Yaqoub ibn Yaqteen said: 'I saw Abu Al-Hasan, meaning Al-Reza (peace be upon him), breaking the bread upwards.'

key_terms.رُغْفَانَكُمْ: Your bread (plural form, implying multiple pieces or loaves)

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual significance of breaking bread into smaller pieces in Shia tradition?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* highlights the spiritual significance of *sadr al-khubz* (breaking bread), linking the physical act of portioning food to the multiplication of divine blessings (*barakah*). It is further validated by the practical example of Imam Al-Reza (AS), whose specific manner of breaking bread underscores the importance of mindful consumption and sharing in Shia etiquette. This practice reflects the broader Islamic principle that gratitude and moderation in sustenance invite spiritual abundance.
